FORECAST PAGE, desktop

Broadsheet layout: masthead, a written lede that says what today is actually like, then hills in three columns under section rules by height band.

The lede is generated from the numbers, not hand-written. It is what makes the page readable rather than a spreadsheet.

HOW TO READ THIS

For a first-time visitor. Three short sections: the one idea, why other forecasts get summits wrong, and why the number is a chance rather than a promise. Then a glossary.

The red-ruled box is deliberate: the forecast is unvalidated and the page says so plainly rather than burying it.
